speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with symptoms specifically triggered by looking up or down, is very characteristic. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or speaking recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The combination of diplopia worsening with extreme gaze, proximal muscle weakness that fluctuates with activity but improves with rest, and the absence of sensory deficits or cranial nerve palsies like dysphonia strongly points to this diagnosis.
